Historical description:

Companion manuscript submitted to Physical Review E (Regular Article, interdisciplinary physics section). The paper applies stochastic thermodynamics and information theory to a question usually treated outside physics: the structure of goal-directed human-AI dialogue.

Building on the Intelligence Bound master inequality (Hart 2025) — which establishes that learning systems are data-limited, sitting 10^11 to 10^16 below the Landauer ceiling — the manuscript models dialogue as adaptive co-measurement and derives three results:

  1. Adaptive questioning is a richness pump. By holding per-sample mutual information near its maximum, an inquiring agent raises the binding "rho dot B" term of the Intelligence Bound, pulling effective dI/dt closer to the thermodynamic ceiling than passive observation can.
  2. Goal-directedness composes additively. The information-yield of a dialogue decomposes into geometric, computational, measurement, decoherence, and mutualistic terms — the same five-component slack accounting derived for the underlying Intelligence Bound (Hart 2026, Zenodo 20320324).
  3. The Wavefunction analogy is mathematical, not metaphysical. The paper uses Hilbert-space formalism strictly as a tool for tracking superposed hypotheses under adaptive measurement; no claim depends on quantum mechanics or on a quantum description of cognition.

Files. co-measurement.pdf (manuscript), co-measurement.tex (LaTeX source, standard article class — APS RevTeX 4.2 port planned for final submission), co-measurement-algorithms.pdf + .tex (algorithmic supplement), cover-letter.pdf + .md (editorial cover letter).

Formal verification. Two layers of machine-checked formalization accompany this submission. (1) The Intelligence Bound itself is formalized in Lean 4 as the P0_IntelligenceBound_COMPILED module of the Viridis Compiled Theorem Stack (concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19317982). (2) The seven non-physical theorems supporting this paper's adaptive-measurement model are released as the Co-Measurement Formal Verification Companion (Zenodo 20399474), with every proof returning only the three standard Lean kernel axioms.

Citation. Hart, J. D. (2026). Co-Measurement: Human-AI Dialogue as an Adaptive Measurement Instrument in the Data-Limited Regime of the Intelligence Bound. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20399676

Part of the Viridis canon. Affiliation: Viridis LLC, Columbia Falls, Montana, USA. Contact: viridisnorthllc@gmail.com.
